newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshi firms punished for alleged manipulation.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi firms punished for alleged manipulation.

text.p: Bangladesh's Securities and Exchange commission (SEC), the market watchdog, has suspended two brokerages from stock trading and fined a firm for alleged involvement in share price manipulation, market officials said on Thursday.
"Formal letters to this effect were sent (to) all of them on Wednesday," an SEC official told Reuters.

Officials said the SEC had suspended the trading licences of Asia Securities Ltd and the Capital Investment and Services Company Ltd, and fined Excelsior Shoes Ltd 100,000 taka ($2,290) for alleged involvement in price manipulation.
The officials alleged that all three were involved in a deal where they used fictitious names in the transaction of 10,000 shares of Excelsior Shoes on February 2.
The 100-taka Excelsior share was traded at 550 taka on February 2. It was traded at 112.61 taka on Wednesday.
Excelsior Shoes is listed on both the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DES) and Chittagong Stock Exchange.
"The alleged manipulators failed to defend themselves when they were summoned before a SEC board on June 19," another SEC official said.
"We have not received the letter yet. We will take steps after seeing the content of the formal letters," said an official with Capital Investment and Services Company Ltd.
"The brokerage firms will not be allowed to trade on the floor from Thursday," a DSE official said. ($ = 43.55 Bangladesh Taka)
